objective: One Corpus Clock Contract: every corpus declares an explicit, configured clock identity (provider / broker / clock_id) whose definition (IANA timezone + server_midnight_local) lives in configs/data_provenance/ohlcv_clock_registry.json; the Corpus SSOT (F-119) normalizes the corpus to canonical UTC exactly once (source_timestamp kept for audit); day/week/HTF grids follow a separate market-calendar contract selected by instrument. feature_pipeline.session_timestamp_basis (F-066/F-117 broker_local|utc_corrected) is retired. Resolves the F-117 fallout: one global basis key could not describe corpora with different clocks (UTC corpora hit 'DOUBLE CONVERSION refused').
change_class_rationale: Dataset identity schema gains required provider/broker/clock_id (DATASET_SCHEMA_CHANGE); candle timestamps, the CRT session filter score_time, calendar grids and trade-record hour/day move to canonical UTC / market calendar (RUNTIME_DECISION_PATH_CHANGE); the retired feature_pipeline key is removed from 12 production configs (PRODUCTION_CONFIG_CHANGE); the corpus SSOT now binds a declared clock to every corpus and a new frozen contract + registry schema 2.0.0 define it (CORPUS_AUTHORITY_CHANGE); run / ledger / event timestamps become canonical UTC (RUN_IDENTITY_CHANGE).
affected_models: none retrained. FM-052 session/hour_of_day values on the ACTIVE config are unchanged (v7 already derived them from true UTC); the shadow/legacy configs that carried session_timestamp_basis=broker_local now read UTC too, so their session / hour_of_day features and CRT session filter move by the 2-3h server offset.
affected_production_config: ACTIVE v2_htfcrt_2026_08: feature_pipeline.session_timestamp_basis removed (was utc_corrected) - behaviour identical (candles are now UTC and the filter compares them directly). 11 other configs: key removed (was broker_local) - their session filter and session/hour_of_day semantics move to UTC. feature_pipeline is a non-params section: params hash unchanged.
behavioral_effects: Candle.timestamp / frame timestamp are canonical UTC; trades, events and ledgers carry UTC stamps (source_timestamp on the SSOT frame).

CRTEngine.score_time (RiskScore.time_score) now compares UTC against UTC-authored windows; before, it compared the RAW broker stamp (a surface the clock_registry docstring listed as inconsistent) - trade scores may move.
BacktestRunner._session (non-exchange basis) compared the raw broker stamp to UTC-authored windows; now UTC vs UTC.
Calendar grids (D1/H4/H1/W1/MN1, PDH/PDL, day_of_week, HTF ids, swap nights) follow market_calendar.json and reproduce the previous broker grid exactly for fx_metals.
engine_runner regime-governor daily quota boundary: UTC date (was broker date).
A corpus with no configured clock identity is refused at SSOT load (7 reviewed MT5 records without a declared server are refused until a human declares them).
unverified_or_deferred: Research artifacts stored in broker time (clean-label surfaces, bar matrices) must be regenerated; joins between UTC bars and old broker-time surfaces will not match.
Semantic OS MKT-C06 parameter name 'session_timestamp_basis' retained as a label of the supplied series' clock (no conversion); vocabulary migration is a separate step.
Crypto/FX corpora other than the 6 Binance M5 files and the XAUUSD windows remain undeclared (refused in production).
authority_granted: User 2026-10-08: explicit configured clock identities, no inference, full migration (Candle.timestamp = UTC), retire session_timestamp_basis, certification tests name the identity they certify.
authority_NOT_granted: No G001 / economic claim; no change to canonical corpus bytes; no review of crypto/FX clocks.
rollback_boundary: Config-reversible only in part: the retired key can be restored on a config, but the SSOT then ignores it. Full rollback = revert the code (clock_contract/clock_registry/corpus_store/market_calendar + consumers), the registry 2.0.0 file, the dataset schema + 3 dataset records, and the 12 configs together; research artifacts regenerated under UTC would then be broker-clock again.
